request.user:
[2023 summer phd probability — problem 3]

Part I, Exercise 3. Let $X$ be valued on $[-1, 1]$ with symmetric density $f$ ($f(x) = f(-x)$). Let $Y$ take values $\pm 1$ with $P(Y = 1 \mid X = x) = \frac{1}{1 + \exp(-x)}$ for every $x \in [-1, 1]$.
Find the density of the random variable $V = YX$.

response.text:
Let

\[
p(x)=P(Y=1\mid X=x)=\frac{1}{1+e^{-x}},
\]

so that

\[
P(Y=-1\mid X=x)=1-p(x)=\frac{1}{1+e^{x}}.
\]

We want the density of

\[
V=YX.
\]

Conditioning on \(X=x\), we have

\[
V=
\begin{cases}
x, & Y=1,\\
-x, & Y=-1.
\end{cases}
\]

Thus for \(v\in[-1,1]\), the density of \(V\) receives contributions from two possibilities:

1. \(X=v\) and \(Y=1\),
2. \(X=-v\) and \(Y=-1\).

Therefore,

\[
f_V(v)
=
f(v)P(Y=1\mid X=v)
+
f(-v)P(Y=-1\mid X=-v).
\]

Using symmetry \(f(-v)=f(v)\), this becomes

\[
f_V(v)
=
f(v)\frac{1}{1+e^{-v}}
+
f(v)\left(1-\frac{1}{1+e^{v}}\right).
\]

But

\[
1-\frac{1}{1+e^{v}}
=
\frac{e^{v}}{1+e^{v}}
=
\frac{1}{1+e^{-v}}.
\]

Hence

\[
f_V(v)
=
2f(v)\frac{1}{1+e^{-v}}.
\]

So the density of \(V\) is

\[
\boxed{
f_V(v)=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{2f(v)}{1+e^{-v}}, & -1\le v\le 1,\\[1.2em]
0, & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
}
\]

As a check, since \(f\) is symmetric and \(p(v)+p(-v)=1\),

\[
\int_{-1}^1 \frac{2f(v)}{1+e^{-v}}\,dv
=
\int_{-1}^1 f(v)\bigl(p(v)+p(-v)\bigr)\,dv
=
\int_{-1}^1 f(v)\,dv
=
1.
\]

Thus this is a valid density.
